old_caption: The video captures a serene and picturesque scene of Lake Louise, nestled between towering mountains. The camera remains stationary throughout the sequence, offering a wide-angle view that emphasizes the vastness and beauty of the landscape. The lake's surface is calm and reflective, mirroring the clear blue sky above and the snow-capped peaks in the distance. On the left side of the frame, dense evergreen forests line the shore, their lush greenery contrasting with the rocky foreground where scattered boulders are visible. In the background, majestic mountains rise, their slopes partially covered in snow, creating a stunning backdrop. The overall atmosphere is tranquil, with no visible movement or activity, allowing viewers to fully absorb the natural splendor of the setting.

caption: The video captures a wide, locked-off view of a glacier-fed alpine lake beneath a snow-covered glacier and rocky peaks. A steep forested cliff and pine slope rise on the left, while a tree-covered mountain slope closes the right side of the valley. In the left foreground, a pale rocky shoreline with scattered boulders meets clear shallow water. The lower-center lake carries a bright white reflection of sky and glacier, and this reflection continuously deforms into shifting horizontal shimmer bands as small ripples pass across the surface. On the right, the transparent water over rounded submerged stones shows subtle ongoing distortion, while a few small red canoes remain at nearly the same positions along the distant horizon. The mountains, forest, shoreline, and framing stay fixed throughout.

endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.
Compare several frames before asserting translation, rotation, direction, unchanged position or
camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

This is a direct video description, not an analysis note. No mandatory beginning/end formula.
